scope: Retrospective event-to-event runtime assessment; not isolated ZK timings or M6 acceptance

customerAssessment.planningEnvelopeScope: Rough risk allowance for similarly sized tested server-side circuit operations on the observed four-CPU profile, including submission/confirmation; not a measured normal-user proof time or larger-circuit upper bound
customerAssessment.enterpriseDirection: Customer-controlled low-frequency asynchronous workloads after missing authorization/security and sustained-load acceptance
customerAssessment.consumerDirection: Requires actual ordinary-action circuit completion and target-device/privacy/latency qualification
remainingProductionRequirements: Complete current-root ancestry/account checks, runtime authorization, atomic state/nullifier updates and common receipt
Pass full required chain negatives, restart/reconnect and sustained memory/load verification
Measure per-proof latency and hardware scaling with exact circuit/key hashes
Optimize circuit or prover if ordinary-action latency/memory exceeds agreed product requirements

qualifications: Intervals include local preparation, all proving/checking, balancing, submission and indexed confirmation, not isolated proof latency.
The first approval interval must start at the last review, not the first review.
Parent/child timing is from an earlier stock-prover run that subsequently OOM-failed during governance; it is not a patched-prover full-workflow pass.
No measured scaling factor from 4 to 8 or 16 CPU cores exists.
The 16 GiB single-worker configuration is an unverified memory-headroom estimate, not a latency guarantee.
derivation: elapsed seconds = (end event timestamp - start event timestamp) / 1000; public milestone events only
